sections.title: 听力
sections.instructions: 录音只播一遍。25 题单选，每题 9.94 分（710 分制，听力共 248.5 分）。

parts.zh: W：你好，请坐。我这里有你的检查结果
M：那我为什么总是感觉这么不舒服？
W：这可能是过度劳累和压力造成的
M：不，不可能。我一直都很努力地工作
W：你刚才描述的情况很常见
M：对，实际上大多数日子都是这样
W：那并不代表什么。你可能在不知情的情况下承受了20年的压力
W：这些都是压力带来的常见后果

questions.stem: What do we learn about the man from his test results?
options: It is clear that he is expected to enjoy a healthy life.
There is nothing wrong with his digestive system.
There is some indication of an issue with his blood circulation.
He doesn't know he has long been suffering from poor health.
optionsZh: 很明显他有望享有健康的生活。
他的消化系统没有任何问题。
有迹象表明他的血液循环存在问题。
他不知道自己长期以来一直健康状况不佳。
questions.explain: 正确答案 B：There is nothing wrong with his digestive system.（他的消化系统没有任何问题。）

questions.stem: What does the woman think is a common phenomenon among many people?
options: Mistaking symptoms of illness for stress.
Complaining they are being overworked.
Being unaware of the stress they are under.
Suffering from illness without recognising it.
optionsZh: 将疾病症状误认为是压力。
抱怨自己工作过度。
没有意识到自己所承受的压力。
患病却没有察觉。
questions.explain: 正确答案 C：Being unaware of the stress they are under.（没有意识到自己所承受的压力。）

questions.stem: What does the woman say she will do for the man?
options: Prescribe some medication for him.
Give him another physical check-up.
Explain to him the common consequence of stress.
Buy some sleeping pills for him from the drugstore.
optionsZh: 给他开一些药物。
再给他做一次体检。
向他解释压力的常见后果。
从药店为他购买一些安眠药。
questions.explain: 正确答案 A：Prescribe some medication for him.（给他开一些药物。）

questions.stem: What does the man say about the industry he is engaged in?
options: It calls for responsible management.
It proves to be quite profitable.
It is remarkably promising.
It is full of competition.
optionsZh: 它要求负责任的管理。
它被证明相当有利可图。
它非常有前景。
它充满竞争。
questions.explain: 正确答案 D：It is full of competition.（它充满竞争。）

questions.stem: Why did John Williams leave the sport of basketball at just 25?
options: To avoid being in the limelight.
To seek medical help for his injury.
To pursue a less competitive career.
To stay away from his hostile teammates.
optionsZh: 为了避免成为公众关注的焦点。
为了寻求医疗帮助治疗他的伤病。
为了追求竞争性较小的职业。
为了远离充满敌意的队友。
questions.explain: 正确答案 A：To avoid being in the limelight.（为了避免成为公众关注的焦点。）

questions.stem: What does the man say about basketball as a career for most players?
options: It has ups and downs.
It proves rewarding.
It does not last long.
It is not so profitable.
optionsZh: 它有起有落。
它被证明是有回报的。
它持续的时间不长。
它没有那么赚钱。
questions.explain: 正确答案 C：It does not last long.（它持续的时间不长。）

questions.stem: What do we learn from the woman about John Williams 20 years later?
options: He was a financial advisor.
He suffered from poor health.
He became a basketball coach.
He was back in the news.
optionsZh: 他是一名财务顾问。
他健康状况不佳。
他成为了一名篮球教练。
他重新出现在新闻中。
questions.explain: 正确答案 D：He was back in the news.（他重新出现在新闻中。）

questions.stem: What has the man spent the last two decades trying to do?
options: Study issues of public health.
Alleviate the obesity problem.
Raise sufficient public funding.
Train young basketball players.
optionsZh: 研究公共卫生问题。
缓解肥胖问题。
筹集足够的公共资金。
训练年轻篮球运动员。
questions.explain: 正确答案 B：Alleviate the obesity problem.（缓解肥胖问题。）

questions.stem: When did Kate Atkinson begin to write for women's magazines?
options: When she started teaching at Edinburgh University in Scotland.
While she was doing her doctoral studies on American Literature.
After publishing her first novel Behind the Scenes at the Museum.
After winning the 1986 Woman's Own Short Story Competition.
optionsZh: 当她开始在苏格兰爱丁堡大学任教时。
在她攻读美国文学博士学位期间。
在出版她的第一部小说《博物馆幕后》之后。
在赢得1986年《女性周刊》短篇小说大赛之后。
questions.explain: 正确答案 D：After winning the 1986 Woman's Own Short Story Competition.（在赢得1986年《女性周刊》短篇小说大赛之后。）

questions.stem: What did Kate Atkinson's books touch on?
options: The themes of love and loss.
The code of human behaviour.
The sins and flaws of eccentrics.
The manners of fashionable circles.
optionsZh: 爱与失去的主题。
人类行为的准则。
古怪之人的罪过和缺陷。
上流社会的礼仪。
questions.explain: 正确答案 A：The themes of love and loss.（爱与失去的主题。）

questions.stem: What do we learn about the clever and deceitful characters in a comedy of manners?
options: They are usually ignorant of complex human relations.
They successfully imitate the manners of celebrities.
They often get rewarded instead of being punished.
They are generally looked down upon in society.
optionsZh: 他们通常对复杂的人际关系一无所知。
他们成功地模仿名人的举止。
他们经常得到奖赏而不是受到惩罚。
他们在社会上普遍受到轻视。
questions.explain: 正确答案 C：They often get rewarded instead of being punished.（他们经常得到奖赏而不是受到惩罚。）

questions.stem: Why does the speaker say adaptability is an important skill to exercise in the workplace?
options: It is what members use to alleviate tension in a team.
It is what employers are increasingly seeking after.
It is conducive to getting over a recession.
It is necessary for learning a new task.
optionsZh: 这是成员用来缓解团队紧张气氛的能力。
这是雇主日益寻求的能力。
这有助于度过经济衰退。
这是学习新任务所必需的。
questions.explain: 正确答案 B：It is what employers are increasingly seeking after.（这是雇主日益寻求的能力。）

questions.stem: What does adaptability enable us to do according to strategy consultant Dorie Clark?
options: Make better choices.
Follow innovative ideas.
Achieve recognition duly.
Accumulate work experience.
optionsZh: 做出更好的选择。
追随创新理念。
及时获得认可。
积累工作经验。
questions.explain: 正确答案 A：Make better choices.（做出更好的选择。）

questions.stem: What do we learn about today's work culture from the passage?
options: Workers show more emotional intelligence.
Workers use brains more than muscles.
People usually work flexible hours.
People often work in teams.
optionsZh: 员工表现出更高的情商。
员工更多使用脑力而非体力。
人们通常采用弹性工作时间。
人们经常以团队形式工作。
questions.explain: 正确答案 D：People often work in teams.（人们经常以团队形式工作。）

questions.stem: What are employees with adaptability able to do when changes occur?
options: Leave the group as soon as possible.
Anticipate setbacks well in advance.
Decide on new priorities speedily.
Stick to original goals confidently.
optionsZh: 尽快离开团队。
提前充分预见挫折。
迅速决定新的优先事项。
自信地坚持原有目标。
questions.explain: 正确答案 C：Decide on new priorities speedily.（迅速决定新的优先事项。）

questions.stem: What question does the speaker address in this talk?
options: What differentiates people from animals.
Why philosophers disagree with scientists.
Where humans' great cognitive capacity originates.
When being creative becomes a biological mandate.
optionsZh: 人与动物的区别是什么。
哲学家为什么不同意科学家的观点。
人类巨大的认知能力源于何处。
创造力何时成为一种生物学上的必然要求。
questions.explain: 正确答案 A：What differentiates people from animals.（人与动物的区别是什么。）

questions.stem: What does the speaker believe about innovation?
options: It is what tells apart two adjacent generations.
It is what sharpens our appetite for novelty.
It is something only geniuses can achieve.
It is something every human being can do.
optionsZh: 它是区分相邻两代人的标志。
它是激发我们对新奇事物渴望的东西。
它是只有天才才能实现的事情。
它是每个人都能做到的事情。
questions.explain: 正确答案 D：It is something every human being can do.（它是每个人都能做到的事情。）

questions.stem: How does the human brain work according to the speaker?
options: It seeks inspiration for novel inventions.
It constantly absorbs new information.
It uses existing ideas to create new ones.
It repeats precedent on a regular basis.
optionsZh: 它为新颖的发明寻找灵感。
它不断吸收新信息。
它利用现有想法创造新想法。
它定期重复先例。
questions.explain: 正确答案 C：It uses existing ideas to create new ones.（它利用现有想法创造新想法。）

questions.stem: What view of many dog owners win support from researchers studying dog cognition?
options: Dogs know when their owners are not feeling well.
Dogs have the cognition for telling right from wrong.
Dogs have an aptitude for developing skills to interact with humans.
Dogs know when their human companions can no longer stand them.
optionsZh: 狗知道它们的主人身体不适。
狗具有辨别是非的认知能力。
狗具有发展与人类互动技能的天赋。
狗知道它们的人类同伴何时无法再忍受它们。
questions.explain: 正确答案 A：Dogs know when their owners are not feeling well.（狗知道它们的主人身体不适。）

questions.stem: Why can dogs detect their owner's abnormal odor according to the speaker?
options: They can readily detect different ill smells of viruses.
They can easily tell what bacteria cause odor change.
They are particularly sensitive to strange smells.
They have an extremely powerful sense of smell.
optionsZh: 它们能轻易探测到病毒的各种病态气味。
它们能容易地辨别出什么细菌导致气味变化。
它们对陌生气味特别敏感。
它们拥有极其强大的嗅觉。
questions.explain: 正确答案 D：They have an extremely powerful sense of smell.（它们拥有极其强大的嗅觉。）

questions.stem: What does research suggest for now about dog ownership?
options: It can ensure owners suffer fewer chronic diseases.
It can benefit owners both physically and mentally.
It can reduce owners' risk of getting cancer or diabetes.
It can alert owners to the seriousness of their conditions.
optionsZh: 它能确保主人较少患慢性疾病。
它能在身体和心理上使主人受益。
它能降低主人患癌症或糖尿病的风险。
它能提醒主人注意其病情的严重性。
questions.explain: 正确答案 B：It can benefit owners both physically and mentally.（它能在身体和心理上使主人受益。）

questions.stem: What does Onward's report propose ministers should do?
options: Crack down on courses like science, technology, engineering and math.
Restrict the ability of creative arts courses to recruit new students.
Look at how to reform technical and vocational education.
Ensure creative arts students get better value for money.
optionsZh: 严厉打击科学、技术、工程和数学等课程。
限制创意艺术课程招收新生的能力。
研究如何改革技术和职业教育。
确保创意艺术专业学生获得更高的性价比。
questions.explain: 正确答案 B：Restrict the ability of creative arts courses to recruit new students.（限制创意艺术课程招收新生的能力。）

questions.stem: What does the speaker think of Onward's arguments?
options: Seemingly reasonable.
Clearly well-grounded.
Extremely irrational.
Apparently simplistic.
optionsZh: 看似合理。
明显有充分根据。
极其不理性。
显然过于简单化。
questions.explain: 正确答案 A：Seemingly reasonable.（看似合理。）

questions.stem: What do we learn about British college graduates five years after graduation?
options: A high proportion of them haven't tried to save money.
Most of them never hope to buy a house or to retire.
Forty percent of them earn less than ￡25,000 a year.
The majority of them have fairly well-paying jobs.
optionsZh: 他们中很大比例没有试图存钱。
他们中的大多数从未希望买房或退休。
他们中40%的人年收入低于25,000英镑。
他们中的大多数拥有薪酬相当不错的工作。
questions.explain: 正确答案 C：Forty percent of them earn less than ￡25,000 a year.（他们中40%的人年收入低于25,000英镑。）

questions.stem: What does the speaker say actually accounts for the problem identified by Onward?
options: The context of a bank balance.
Britain's economy as a whole.
The specific degree a student earns.
Britain's defective educational system.
optionsZh: 银行余额的背景。
英国整体经济。
学生获得的具体学位。
英国有缺陷的教育体系。
questions.explain: 正确答案 B：Britain's economy as a whole.（英国整体经济。）

sections.title: 写作
sections.instructions: 真题 Part Ⅰ · 30 分钟 · 150–210 词

items.prompt: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence "As is known to all, gaining a sound knowledge of the basics is of vital importance for students to master an academic subject.”You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words (not including the sentence given).
items.rubric: CET 写作 15 分制（六级）：切题、篇章连贯、用词准确

sections.title: 选词填空
sections.instructions: 真题 Part Ⅲ Section A · 15 选 10 · 10 空

items.stem: The desert is deceiving. At first glance it looks lifeless, barren, and bone-dry. For most passersby humming through the Mojave on their way to try their luck in Las Vegas or heading towards the Grand Canyon, it's just a {{1}} stretch of land with some mountains in the distance and more {{2}} to be a setting for a movie that takes place on Mars. The desert, however, is {{3}} with life, mystery, and magic. The Mojave desert sees less than two inches of rain a year, and like most deserts, is a land of {{4}} . Temperature fluctuations vary from freezing to {{5}} hot, not only between seasons, but even within the same day. At the heart of this vast, 25,000-square-mile desert is Mojave National Preserve. The folks managing and working there wear the wide-brimmed(宽边的) hats that have become {{6}} with places like Yosemite. The preserve is rich with history, culture, biodiversity, and endless opportunities to {{7}} your interest, especially for anyone who loves the outdoors. For a photographer, it requires patience and {{8}} a few spare tires to maneuver the network of unpaved "roads", but the rewards are plenty. Photographing here requires a good, {{9}} pair of shoes and a lot of preparation. Plenty of water, spare tires, and a full tank of gas are needed to explore this unit of the national park system, which is the third largest in the country. Like all deserts, though, if you are patient, you will be rewarded, as they often reveal their secrets slowly. During my last outing, I was surprised to see how much of the area was shaped by ancient volcanoes and geological forces, much of which remains today, giving the area a {{10}} feel and painting a colorful background for great photographs.
options: apt
burning
extremes
flat
fractions
overflowing
parasites
probably
sparingly
sprinkle
steer
stimulate
sturdy
synonymous
unique
blankExplains:
【定位】For most passersby humming through the Mojave on their way to try their luck in Las Vegas or heading towards the Grand Canyon, it's just a ____ stretch of land with some mountains in the distance and more  … to be a setting for a movie that takes place on Mars.
【依据】答案是 flat：填回后与所在句 passersby、humming、through、mojave、way、try 构成完整表达，词性与该空位置吻合（本句需要一个与整段话题一致的实词）。按词性先分组、再按搭配与语义场排除，是这一题型唯一可靠的顺序。

【定位】For most passersby humming through the Mojave on their way to try their luck in Las Vegas or heading towards the Grand Canyon, it's just a  … stretch of land with some mountains in the distance and more ____ to be a setting for a movie that takes place on Mars.
【依据】答案是 apt：填回后与所在句 passersby、humming、through、mojave、way、try 构成完整表达，词性与该空位置吻合（本句需要一个与整段话题一致的实词）。按词性先分组、再按搭配与语义场排除，是这一题型唯一可靠的顺序。

【定位】The desert, however, is ____ with life, mystery, and magic.
【依据】答案是 overflowing：填回后与所在句 desert、however、life、mystery、magic 构成完整表达，词性与该空位置吻合（本句需要一个与整段话题一致的实词）。按词性先分组、再按搭配与语义场排除，是这一题型唯一可靠的顺序。

【定位】The Mojave desert sees less than two inches of rain a year, and like most deserts, is a land of ____ .
【依据】答案是 extremes：填回后与所在句 mojave、desert、sees、less、two、inches 构成完整表达，词性与该空位置吻合（本句需要一个与整段话题一致的实词）。按词性先分组、再按搭配与语义场排除，是这一题型唯一可靠的顺序。

【定位】Temperature fluctuations vary from freezing to ____ hot, not only between seasons, but even within the same day.
【依据】答案是 burning：填回后与所在句 temperature、fluctuations、vary、freezing、hot、only 构成完整表达，词性与该空位置吻合（本句需要一个与整段话题一致的实词）。按词性先分组、再按搭配与语义场排除，是这一题型唯一可靠的顺序。

【定位】The folks managing and working there wear the wide-brimmed(宽边的) hats that have become ____ with places like Yosemite.
【依据】答案是 synonymous：填回后与所在句 folks、managing、working、there、wear、wide-brimmed 构成完整表达，词性与该空位置吻合（本句需要一个与整段话题一致的实词）。按词性先分组、再按搭配与语义场排除，是这一题型唯一可靠的顺序。

【定位】The preserve is rich with history, culture, biodiversity, and endless opportunities to ____ your interest, especially for anyone who loves the outdoors.
【依据】答案是 stimulate：填回后与所在句 preserve、rich、history、culture、biodiversity、endless 构成完整表达，词性与该空位置吻合（本句需要一个与整段话题一致的实词）。按词性先分组、再按搭配与语义场排除，是这一题型唯一可靠的顺序。

【定位】For a photographer, it requires patience and ____ a few spare tires to maneuver the network of unpaved "roads", but the rewards are plenty.
【依据】答案是 probably：填回后与所在句 photographer、requires、patience、few、spare、tires 构成完整表达，词性与该空位置吻合（本句需要一个与整段话题一致的实词）。按词性先分组、再按搭配与语义场排除，是这一题型唯一可靠的顺序。

【定位】Photographing here requires a good, ____ pair of shoes and a lot of preparation.
【依据】答案是 sturdy：填回后与所在句 photographing、here、requires、good、pair、shoes 构成完整表达，词性与该空位置吻合（本句需要一个与整段话题一致的实词）。按词性先分组、再按搭配与语义场排除，是这一题型唯一可靠的顺序。

【定位】During my last outing, I was surprised to see how much of the area was shaped by ancient volcanoes and geological forces, much of which remains today, giving the area a ____ feel and painting a colorful background for great photographs.
【依据】答案是 unique：填回后与所在句 during、last、outing、surprised、see、how 构成完整表达，词性与该空位置吻合（本句需要一个与整段话题一致的实词）。按词性先分组、再按搭配与语义场排除，是这一题型唯一可靠的顺序。
items.explain: 本段为选词填空，共 10 空，候选词 15 个。解题顺序是：先通读判断体裁与话题 → 按词性给候选词分组 → 逐空用搭配与语义场排除。15 选 10 意味着有 5 个候选词永远用不上，遇到"读起来也通顺"的选项时要看它是否破坏了整段的一致性。

paragraphs.text: On the hills of central Kenya, almost lime-green with the sparkle of tea bushes in the sunlight, farmers know all about climate change. "The rainy season is no longer predictable," says one. "When it is supposed to rain it doesn't, then it all comes at once." Climate change is an issue that will affect everyone on the planet. For Africans its consequences will be particularly bitter: whereas other regions were able to grow rich by burning coal and oil, Africa will pay much of the human price without having enjoyed the benefits. "Africa only represents 2% of global greenhouse-gas emissions but it is the continent that is expected to suffer the most from climate impacts," says Mafalda Duarte, who runs the World Bank's $8bn Climate Investment Funds.

Although there are huge uncertainties as to the precise impacts of climate change, enough is known to say that global warming represents one of the main threats to Africa's prosperity. Parts of the continent are already warming much more quickly than the average: temperatures in southern Africa have increased by about twice the global rate over the past 50 years. Even if the world were to cut emissions enough to keep global warming below 1.5℃, heat-waves would intensify in Africa and diseases would spread to areas not currently affected. Farming would also be hit hard. About 40% of the land now used to grow maize(玉米) would no longer be suitable for it. Overall, it is estimated that maize yields would fall by 18-22%.

Africa is particularly vulnerable, in part because it is already struggling to feed itself and it will have to vastly increase yields and productivity if it is to put food on the plates of a fast-growing population, even without climate change. The UN's Food and Agriculture Organisation reckons that by 2050 global food production would have to rise by about 70% over its level of 2009 to meet demand from a population that is growing in numbers and appetite. Much of this new demand will be in Africa. Yet the continent already imports about $50bn-worth of food a year and that figure is expected to more than double over the next five years. Self-sufficiency is not Africa's goal, but the fact that it spends more money importing food than it does buying capital goods suggests it has room for improvement.

Finding out why is not hard. Most farms are tiny, ploughed by hand and reliant on rain. More than half of Africa's people make their living from farming. Although its total harvest has climbed over the past few decades, this is mainly because there are more people farming more land. But in many places there is no spare land to farm. Plots in Rwanda are so small that you could fit 250 of them onto the average American farm. And although output per worker has improved by more than half over the past 30 years in Africa, that is still far behind the 2.5 times improvement in Asia. Yields of maize are generally less than two tonnes per hectare, a fifth the level in America.

The low productivity of African farmers is reflected in national economic statistics—despite absorbing so much labour, farming generates just 15% of GDP. "They can't even feed their families," says Jennifer Blanke, a vice-president of the African Development Bank in charge of agriculture. "Farm productivity hasn't improved in many parts of Africa for 100 years."

One reason is that in the first few decades of independence, many African governments neglected farming as they focused on industrialising their economies. Others damaged it by pushing down the prices that state monopolies paid for their crops in order to subsidise workers in cities with cheap food. Ghana taxed cocoa(可可粉) exports so heavily that production collapsed by half between the 1960s and 1980s, despite a jump in the global price of cocoa. Yet over the past two decades or so governments and donors have begun to look again at farming as a way of providing jobs for the 13 million young people entering the workforce each year. Much of the focus has been on getting small farmers to use fertiliser and, more important, better seeds. The results can be impressive. Improved varieties of sorghum(高梁), for instance, can produce a crop that is 40% larger than the usual variety. Infrastructure is important. A World Bank irrigation project in Ethiopia helped farmers increase their potato harvest from about 8 tonnes per hectare to 35 tonnes.

Better techniques help, too. Small coffee farmers in Kenya are able to increase their incomes by 40% by following a few simple guidelines on caring for their bushes, such as trimming all but three of their stems. Many of their neighbours do not follow the advice, because it seems counter-intuitive. More stems ought to lead to more coffee beans, they say. Yet after seeing those following the advice get bigger harvests for a season or two, many others start doing the same.

One way of spreading knowledge is to link farms to big buyers of their harvests. When Diageo, a British drinks giant, built a brewery in western Kenya, it wanted to use local crops to make a beer cheap enough to compete with illicit home brew. It organised farmers into groups, improved supply chains for them to get seeds and fertiliser and then agreed to buy their grain. It now provides a market to about 17,000 farmers. Across the region it has doubled its use of local raw material to about 80% over five years, says John O'Keeffe, who runs its Africa business.

An even more important change is the move from traditional farming to building businesses that can profitably bring technology and investment to small farmers. Taita Ngetich, a young Kenyan, was studying engineering when he wanted to earn a little money on the side. He scraped together 20,000 Kenyan shillings (about $200) to plant tomatoes. Everything went wrong. The crop was attacked by pests. "Then there was a massive flood that swallowed all our capital," he says. Mr Ngetich persevered by looking into buying a greenhouse to protect his plants from bugs and rain. The cheapest ones cost more than $2,500 each, so he designed his own for half the price. Soon neighbouring farmers started placing orders with him, and now his firm, Illuminum Greenhouses, has sold more than 1,400 greenhouses that provide livelihoods to about 6,000 people. The business does not stop there; he also supplies fertiliser, high-quality seedlings and smart sensors that increase yields.

Illuminum's success shows how technology can help even small farms become more productive. Because such a large share of Africa's population earns a living from agriculture, even small improvements in productivity can lift the incomes of millions of people. But over the longer run small-scale farming can go only so far, especially in the face of climate change and population pressure.

"If we really want to lift people out of poverty we have to finance projects that will get them an income of at least $100 a month so that they can pay for health care and education," says Mr Ngetich. "Projects that give them an extra $2 a month from growing beans or maize aren't going to get them there." Getting those big jumps will need better jobs in factories and cities.

statements.text: It is said that agricultural productivity in many African countries has remained low for a century.
Building connections between farms and major purchasers of their produce can promote African farmers' use of advanced farming techniques.
Parts of Africa are getting warmer much faster than the average, with southern Africa witnessing roughly twice the global warming rate over the last half century.
Improved farming practices have enabled Kenyan farmers to increase farm produce remarkably.
Africa is especially susceptible to the effects of global warming partly because it has difficulty feeding its increasing population even without climate change.
The use of fertiliser and improved seeds can help Africa's small farmers impressively increase crop yields.
It has proved even more important to shift from traditional farming to setting up businesses that can bring technology and investment to small farmers in Africa.
Everyone in the world will have to bear the consequences of climate change, especially Africans.
Improvement in farm output per worker in Africa falls far short of that in Asia.
In the long term, the potential for small farms in Africa to increase productivity is quite limited, especially owing to the warming climate and a growing population.

sections.instructions: 真题 Part Ⅲ Section C · 2 篇 × 5 题

items.passage: One of the great successes of the Republican Party in recent decades is the relentless propagation of a simple formula for economic growth: tax cuts. The formula doesn't work, but that has not affected its popularity. And while the cult of tax cuts has attracted many critics, it lacks for obvious rivals. Democratic politicians have tended to campaign on helping people left behind by economic growth. When Democrats do talk about encouraging economic growth, they often sound like Republicans. This is not just a political problem for Democrats; it is an economic problem for the United States. The nation needs a better story about the drivers of economic growth. The painful lessons of recent decades point to a promising candidate: higher wages. Raising the wages of American workers ought to be the priority of economic policymakers. We'd all be better off paying less attention to quarterly updates on the growth of the nation's gross domestic product (GDP) and focusing instead on the growth of workers' paychecks. Set aside, for the moment, the familiar argument for higher wages: fairness. The argument here is that higher wages can fuel the engine of economic growth. Perhaps the most famous illustration of the benefits is the story of Henry Ford's decision in 1914 to pay $5 a day to workers on his Model T assembly lines. He did it to increase production—he was paying a premium to maintain a reliable workforce. The unexpected benefit was that Ford's factory workers became Ford customers, too. The same logic still holds: Consumption drives the American economy, and workers who are paid more can spend more. Mainstream economists insist that it is impossible to order up a sustainable increase in wages because compensation levels reflect the unerring judgment of market forces. The conventional wisdom held that productivity growth was the only route to higher wages. Through that lens, efforts to negotiate higher wages were counterproductive. Minimum-wage laws would raise unemployment because there was only so much money in the wage pool, and if some people got more, others would get none. It was in the context of this worldview that it became popular to argue that tax cuts would drive prosperity. Rich people would invest, productivity would increase, wages would rise. In the real world, things are more complicated. Wages are influenced by a tug of war between employers and workers, and employers have been winning. One clear piece of evidence is the widening gap between productivity growth and wage growth since roughly 1970. Productivity has more than doubled; wages have lagged far behind. A focus on wage growth would provide an antidote(矫正方法) to the attractive simplicity of the belief in the magical power of tax cuts.

questions.stem: Why does the formula of tax cuts remain popular though ineffective?
options: Its critics' voice has not been heard throughout the country.
There seem to be no other options available to replace it.
The cult of tax cuts has been relentlessly propagated by all policymakers.
There appears to be a misunderstanding of the formula among the public.

items.passage: Journal editors decide what gets published and what doesn't, affecting the careers of other academics and influencing the direction that a field takes. You'd hope, then, that journals would do everything they can to establish a diverse editorial board, reflecting a variety of voices, experiences, and identities. Unfortunately a new study in Nature Neuroscience makes for disheartening reading. The team finds that the majority of editors in top psychology and neuroscience journals are male and based in the United States: a situation that may be amplifying existing gender inequalities in the field and influencing the kind of research that gets published. Men were found to account for 60% of the editors of psychology journals. There were significantly more male than female editors at each level of seniority, and men made up the majority of editors in over three quarters of the journals. Crucially, the proportion of female editors was significantly lower than the overall proportion of women psychology researchers. The differences were even starker in the neuroscience journals: 70% of editors were male, and men held the majority of editorial positions in 88% of journals. In this case, the proportion of female editors was not significantly lower than the proportion of female researchers working in neuroscience—a finding that reveals enduring gender disparities in the field more broadly. Based on their results, the team concludes that "the ideas, values and decision-making biases of men are overrepresented in the editorial positions of the most recognized academic journals in psychology and neuroscience." Gender inequality in science is often attributed to the fact that senior academics are more likely to be male, because historically science was male-dominated: it's argued that as time goes on and more women rise to senior roles, the field will become more equal. Yet this study showed that even the junior roles in psychology journals tended to be held disproportionately by men, despite the fact that there are actually more female than male junior psychology faculty. This implies that a lack of female academics is not the problem. Instead, there are structural reasons that women are disadvantaged in science. Women receive lower salaries and face greater childcare demands, for instance, which can result in fewer publications and grants—the kinds of things that journals look for when deciding who to appoint. Rather than simply blaming the inequality of editorial boards on tradition, we should be actively breaking down these existing barriers. A lack of diversity among journal editors also likely contributes to psychology's WEIRD problem. If journal editors are largely men from the United States, then they will probably place higher value on papers that are relevant to Western, male populations, whether consciously or not.

items.zh: 在中国，随着老龄化社会的到来，养老受到普遍关注。人们谈论最多的是应当采取什么样的养老模式。多数人认为，养老模式需要多元化。可以通过政府引导和社会参与，建立更多更好的养老服务机构，改进社区服务中心，鼓励居家自助养老，还可以推行家庭养老与社会养老相结合的模式。随着政府和社会对养老服务事业投入的持续增加，养老设施将不断升级，服务质量逐步改进，老年人的生活将会更加方便舒适、健康快乐。
